run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T06:07:41Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend is explained by a rollout restart of the ad service (and, secondarily, payment) at 06:06:37–06:06:38 UTC, one minute before the alert fired at 06:07:41. Both deployments were recreated with the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation and identical image/env/resources; the new ad pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 started its container at 06:06:40 but the ad application only logged 'Ad service starting.' at 06:11:20 and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 06:13:00. Neither ad nor payment has a readiness/liveness/startup probe, so the pods were Ready immediately and received traffic before the applications were listening. Frontend error spans, which were exactly zero in every 5-minute window from 05:07:41 through 06:02:41, appear in the window ending 06:07:41 and are dominated by the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client span and the GET /api/data route (407.68 errors each over 05:26:40–06:26:40); between 06:10:40 and 06:14:40 every sampled GetAds call failed (154.67 and 148 errors with 0 non-error calls). The frontend also surfaced POST /api/checkout errors (79.3) that trace to checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client span (64 errors in the 06:08:40–06:09:40 minute), i.e. to payment's simultaneous restart. Ad's own span volume is absent for the buckets ending 06:10:40, 06:12:40 and 06:14:40 and resumes in the bucket ending 06:16:40, matching the frontend error burst; frontend errors fall back to zero in the bucket ending 06:18:40. A separate flagd-config ConfigMap currently carries adFailure=on and paymentUnreachable=on, but its incident-time value could not be verified and ad produced no error spans of its own, so it remains an unconfirmed secondary hypothesis rather than the demonstrated mechanism. A fraud-detection OOM restart at 06:08:25 is a separate change with no observed error evidence tying it to this alert.

claims.text: Frontend error spans (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, service_name="frontend", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR") were 0 in every 5-minute window from 05:07:41 to 06:02:41, then 4.44 in the window ending 06:07:41, 291.11 in the window ending 06:12:41 and 150 in the window ending 06:17:41, giving a clean pre-incident baseline of zero errors.

Over 05:26:40–06:26:40 the frontend's error spans are concentrated in grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (407.68) and the GET /api/data route and its api-route span (407.68 each); POST /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder each show 79.3 errors and tcp.connect 15.25. All other frontend operations are STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

At 2-minute resolution the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds calls show 5.99 errors (06:06:40–06:08:40), 136 errors vs 85.33 non-error (06:08:40–06:10:40), 154.67 errors with 0 non-error (06:10:40–06:12:40), 148 errors with 0 non-error (06:12:40–06:14:40), 35.93 errors vs 29.94 non-error (06:14:40–06:16:40) and 0 errors (06:16:40–06:18:40); every sampled ad call failed during 06:10:40–06:14:40.

Deployment ad was rolled out at 06:06:38: the new ReplicaSet ad-5f8dd7c58d carries template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T06:06:38Z and the old ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 was scaled to 0 and its pod deleted at 06:06:40; image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad), environment and resources (cpu limit 50m) are identical between the old and new ReplicaSet templates.

Deployment payment was rolled out the same way at 06:06:37 (new ReplicaSet payment-5d565cf9b with restartedAt=2026-11-15T06:06:37Z, old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 deleted at 06:06:41), again with identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, environment and resources (cpu limit 20m).

The replacement ad pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 had its container started at 06:06:40 and was reported Ready with condition time 06:06:40, yet the ad application logged 'Ad service starting.' only at 06:11:20 and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 06:13:00, with the first request-handling lines ('no baggage found in context') at 06:14:22.

The ad and payment deployment container specs have no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe (all null), so pods are placed in Service endpoints as soon as the container starts even though the ad JVM was not listening until 06:13:00.

Ad service span volume collapses after the restart: ad's STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans are 284 in the bucket ending 06:06:40, 167.67 in the bucket ending 06:08:40, then 0 for the buckets ending 06:10:40, 06:12:40 and 06:14:40, and resume at 211.38 in the bucket ending 06:16:40; the only ad error spans in 05:26:40–06:26:40 are 2.36 on flagd operations (EventStream/ResolveBoolean), with no oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error spans.

Checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client span reports 64 errors in the single 1-minute window 06:08:40–06:09:40 and 0 errors in every later minute up to 06:17:40, while payment's own server spans carry no error status (payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR is 0 throughout).
frontend-proxy recorded its own error spans during the incident: ingress 381.82 and 'router frontend egress' 377.45 in the 6-minute bucket ending 06:12:40, versus 0 in the bucket ending 06:06:40.

Among services that returned error-status series for 06:00:40–06:26:40, frontend had 1991.06 error spans, frontend-proxy 1013.57, checkout 152, ad 2.36, recommendation 2.06, and accounting, fraud-detection and payment 0; the affected entities with their own failure evidence are frontend, checkout and frontend-proxy.

By the end of the window the burst had passed: at 06:26:40 the trailing 12 minutes (06:14:40–06:26:40) contain only 29.37 residual frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds / GET /api/data errors, 0 checkout PlaceOrder and Charge errors, and 0 frontend POST /api/checkout errors, and the 2-minute bucket 06:16:40–06:18:40 shows 0 frontend error spans.
The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg has been running since 05:33:50 with 0 restarts and Ready=true, so the frontend itself was not restarted or crashed during the window.

The flagd-config ConfigMap, read at ~06:27, contains flags with defaultVariant "on" for adFailure ("Fail ad service") and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable"); this is the object's state at query time, not proof of its value during the incident.

The fraud-detection pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n79gv has restartCount 1, lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137, and kubelet Created/Started container events at 06:08:25 during the incident window.

Primary cause: the deliberate rollout restart of Deployment ad at 06:06:38 replaced the only ad pod with one whose application was not listening until 06:13:00 ('Ad service started, listening on 8080'), while the pod was already Ready and had no readiness probe, so frontend gRPC calls to ad:8080 failed (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds errors, 100% failure 06:10:40–06:14:40) and the frontend's GET /api/data route returned errors; this pushed the frontend request error rate above zero from the 06:07:41 alert bucket onward. Ad's missing span volume and its startup log timing coincide exactly with the frontend error burst, and both stop together after ad begins serving (spans resume in the bucket ending 06:16:40).

Secondary contributor: the simultaneous rollout restart of Deployment payment at 06:06:37 briefly removed working payment capacity (errors only in the 06:08:40–06:09:40 minute, 64 failed checkout->payment Charge calls), which made checkout return PlaceOrder errors and produced the frontend POST /api/checkout error spans counted toward the same frontend error-rate alert; payment's first available log lines in the window are at 06:10:01 and it shows no error spans of its own.

Unresolved alternative/secondary cause: the feature flags adFailure ("Fail ad service") and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable") are set to defaultVariant "on" in the current flagd-config ConfigMap and, if they were in that state during the incident, could independently fail frontend->ad and checkout->payment calls. Their incident-time values could not be verified (no flagd metric series exist, the flagd pod produced no readable logs, and flagd loads a file seeded by its init-config container at pod start 05:35:47), and the demonstrated outage phase has ad producing no spans at all rather than error spans, so this is not proven.

The fraud-detection OOMKilled restart at 06:08:25 is not supported as a cause of the frontend error-rate alert: frontend error spans were already present in the bucket ending 06:07:41 before that restart, fraud-detection has 0 error spans in 06:00:40–06:26:40, and no failing frontend or checkout operation implicates fraud-detection. Its restart is a separate event during the window, not observed impact of this cause.

The frontend itself was not the origin of its errors: the frontend pod ran since 05:33:50 with 0 restarts and Ready=true, and its error spans are client spans for grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder plus the /api/data and /api/checkout route spans, i.e. failures of downstream calls, not a frontend restart or crash.

Add a startup/readiness probe (gRPC health on port 8080) to the ad and payment containers so the Service stops routing to a pod whose application is not yet listening, and raise the ad container CPU limit above the current 50m (and payment above 20m) because the ad app needed about 6 minutes from container start to 'listening on 8080'.

Identify who/what issued the kubectl rollout restart at 06:06:37–06:06:38 for ad and payment, and confirm whether the flagd-config adFailure/paymentUnreachable flags were intentionally set to "on" and whether flagd was actually serving those values, before treating the restart alone as the whole story.

gaps: Jaeger trace data ends at 2026-11-15T05:51:14Z (source_end_at of the frontend trace search), before the 06:06–06:16 error burst: traces_search for frontend after 06:22:00 and traces_search_by_tags with service=frontend, operation=grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, tags error=true, 06:00–06:26:40 both returned no data, and the only large trace result was over the size limit and not adopted, so the exact error message/status detail of the failing GetAds and Charge calls is unknown.

Alert definition not verifiable: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rule, so the alert's expression, threshold and current firing/resolved state could not be checked; only the Alertmanager annotation value 4.4222 is known.

Frontend application logs are not readable: both frontend log reads (unfiltered and error-filtered, 06:00–06:26:40) returned 0 bytes with the container stream in 'read' state and no previous instance, so the frontend's own error text and any frontend-side explanation are unknown.

The incident-time value of the flagd flags is unknown: the adFailure/paymentUnreachable values were read from the live ConfigMap at ~06:27 (after the burst), no flagd metric names exist ({__name__=~"flagd.*|.*flag.*" returned nothing), and the flagd pod's logs were unreadable, so it cannot be verified whether those flags were already "on" during 06:06–06:16 or whether flagd was serving them at all.
Change history is not integrated, so what initiated the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt rollouts of ad and payment at 06:06:37/06:06:38 (operator, pipeline or chaos action) is unknown.
Kubernetes events returned only from 06:06:37 onward for the namespace, so earlier conditions (for example the 05:35:47 flagd rollout seen only as a ReplicaSet) are unknown.

Impact on services outside the returned error series is unchecked: cart, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, product-catalog, quote, shipping and load-generator returned no error-status series in 06:00:40–06:26:40, which is unknown rather than zero; the ad logs also could not be filtered for error text over the whole window (the filtered read returned no matching lines only for the 06:15:14–06:16:25 slice that was available).
next_steps: Review the change/rollout record for the ad and payment deployments around 2026-11-15T06:06:37–06:06:38Z to confirm intent and whether the restart was expected.
Verify the values flagd was actually serving during 06:06–06:16 (flags adFailure and paymentUnreachable) and whether the ConfigMap edit preceded or followed the restarts.
Confirm the alert's expression and current state in the Alertmanager/Prometheus that owns it, since the RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in this Prometheus.
Consider a readiness gate on ad/payment and a larger ad CPU limit so a restart cannot route traffic to a non-listening application again.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
